A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PolyGraph Discrepancy work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original perturbation experiments, generative-model benchmarks, training analyses, and sample-size studies in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical studies and adds descriptor-concatenation and graph-kernel classifier comparisons in Appendices Q–R.

M1.justification: The default JS objective, four-fold descriptor selection, and held-out evaluation remain unchanged. v2 adds graph-kernel logistic-regression PGD and evaluates a concatenated-descriptor variant previously suggested as a possible remedy for information loss.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same procedural graph families, Proteins, Citeseer ego graphs, GuacaMol, and MOSES, with the same perturbation scenarios. The new variant comparisons use existing datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: Tables 24–25 add comparisons against PGD-Concat and graph-kernel logistic-regression PGD using PyramidMatch, shortest-path, and Weisfeiler–Lehman kernels. Existing MMD and ordinary logistic-regression comparisons and the four-model GGM benchmark lineup are retained.

E3.justification: Section 5.4 changes the stated procedural benchmark size from 2048 to 4096 graphs. However, Appendix K retains 2048-graph subsamples and Table 18 already listed 4096 test graphs in v1, so this does not establish an actual doubling of evaluation samples. The reported timing hardware also changes.

E4.justification: Appendices Q–R substantially extend tests of two central design choices: whether concatenating descriptors captures information missed by max-reduction, and whether graph-kernel logistic regression provides competitive divergence estimates. Tables 24–25 report these comparisons across four datasets and four generators.

E5.justification: Both retain benchmark means and standard deviations from ten half-dataset subsamples, and the existing resampling and quantile reporting for stability studies. Updated uncertainty values and additional result rows do not establish a new statistical procedure; Table 12 merely removes the stray 'CI' wording.

E6.justification: Numerous correlation, benchmark, timing, and reference estimates change. For example, Table 4 revises AutoGraph's Proteins PGD from 67.7 ± 7.4 to 57.3 ± 11.5, on the displayed percentage scale. Tables 24–25 add variant results, while Table 11 replaces VUN and several PGD entries with dashes. These are revised or newly reported results, not demonstrated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(17), the MMD classification-risk derivation, and the total-variation variational proof retain their mathematical substance. The new variants introduce no additional formal derivation or theorem.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's four contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: interpretable unit-scale classifier-based discrepancy, descriptor comparability, empirical validation, and an evaluation library with larger procedural datasets.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies MMD boundedness and acknowledges that maximizing over bandwidths makes the final estimates biased. It explains differences between cross-validation subscores and held-out PGD, adds the concatenation-versus-attribution tradeoff, and revises feature-dimensionality limitations for TabPFN v2.5.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies TabPFN v2.5. Appendix K changes the reported timing configuration from an L40S with 46 GB GPU memory and 512 GB RAM to an H100 with 80 GB GPU memory and 128 GB RAM. Core pseudocode, descriptor specifications, dataset-generation instructions, and repository access remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds foundational MMD references by Borgwardt et al. and Gretton et al. (2006), plus references supporting the three graph kernels. The overall research positioning remains; publication-year and venue updates for existing works are bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: The introduction and experimental discussion receive localized rewrites, terminology shifts toward 'scores,' and author/header text changes. The main narrative structure remains, and the LLM-use disclosure moves from Appendix Q to S rather than disappearing.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 24–25, restructures several existing tables, relocates displays, and adjusts plot legends, labels, and captions. Tables 12–13 remove their PGD and VUN columns. The overall figure organization and document layout remain recognizable.

improvement.justification: The added aggregation and kernel-classifier analyses strengthen evidence about PGD's design choices, while clearer qualifications of MMD and subscore interpretation improve precision. These gains are limited by reporting regressions: Table 25's PGD values differ from Table 4 despite its caption claiming correspondence, and Table 11 loses comparison entries.
